subject: Mapping evidence provenance & single-owner handback for Whistic profile
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Chen <paul.chen@edgeguard.io>, EdgeGuard Security <security@edgeguard.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mapping evidence provenance & single-owner handback for Whistic profile

Hi Paul / EdgeGuard team —

Thanks for starting the Whistic intake. Before we accept the profile into our vendor inventory, we need to map each evidence artifact to a provenance and a single Redwood owner for ongoing renewals. This prevents orphaned documents during our next evidence rotation and speeds revalidation.

Quick ask: can you confirm which of the artifacts you uploaded are generated by EdgeGuard vs. those produced by shared vendors (e.g., cloud provider SOC reports)? For example: which file should we treat as canonical for encryption-at-rest controls vs. 3rd-party attestation?

Attached: evidence_provenance_matrix.csv (stub with columns: artifact, source, canonical_owner, last_updated, whistic_link). I populated a starter row for the SOC 2 report.

Our proposed process (2-week timeline):
- EdgeGuard to flag canonical artifacts and add an owner contact (name + email) for each artifact in the matrix.
- Redwood to set the Whistic "Profile Owner" field to a single team email and map docs in our inventory.
- For CAIQ/SIG questions that reference evidence, mark the specific artifact in the Whistic answer (link or filename).

Can you take a pass on the matrix by EOD Wed (July 21)? Monica will coordinate the Whistic updates on our side.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Mina Haddad
Vendor Risk Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence_provenance_matrix.csv

From: Paul Chen <paul.chen@edgeguard.io>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeGuard Security <security@edgeguard.io>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 12:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Mapping evidence provenance & single-owner handback for Whistic profile

Thanks Mina — looping in our security ops inbox and responding with the requested mapping.

Quick answers:
- Canonical artifacts: EdgeGuard maintains the canonical SOC 2 Type II report and our internal Key Management Policy. Cloud provider attestations (AWS SOC, Google CAIQ excerpts) are third-party; we referenced them in our answers but they remain provider-owned.
- Owner: I will be the primary owner for EdgeGuard artifacts (Paul Chen, Security Lead — paul.chen@edgeguard.io). For cloud provider docs we included the vendor contact where available.

I attached a short overview (EdgeGuard-SOC2-overview.pdf) and we'll populate the CSV by tomorrow morning. Two clarifications:
1) Does Redwood want us to upload the canonical PDFs into Whistic directly or provide links to our S3 bucket?
2) For CAIQ/Consensus items that point to multiple artifacts, do you prefer us to 1) link to a single canonical file, or 2) list multiple supporting files in the answer?

Happy to hop on a 20-minute call if that speeds things up.

— Paul
Paul Chen
Security Lead, EdgeGuard
paul.chen@edgeguard.io

Attachments: EdgeGuard-SOC2-overview.pdf

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Chen <paul.chen@edgeguard.io>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, EdgeGuard Security <security@edgeguard.io>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mapping evidence provenance & single-owner handback for Whistic profile

Paul — thanks, this is perfect. A couple quick process notes from Redwood's side so expectations are clear:

Process we follow for Whistic onboarding/profiles:
- Preferred: vendor uploads canonical PDFs into Whistic and flags the artifact as "canonical". This gives our procurement/reviewers direct access without S3 permissions friction.
- Alternate: vendor provides a signed URL (1-year expiry minimum) per artifact plus an owner contact; Redwood will mirror the file into our evidence archive and set the Whistic link to the mirrored copy.

For your two questions:
- We prefer vendors upload into Whistic when possible. If not possible, provide signed URLs and we will mirror.
- For CAIQ items that reference multiple supporting artifacts, please indicate one canonical artifact in the matrix and list the supporting artifacts in the "notes" column. That canonical artifact is what our auditors will pull during a review.

Action items & owners:
- Paul / EdgeGuard: populate evidence_provenance_matrix.csv and upload canonical artifacts to Whistic (or provide signed URLs) by EOD Wed (2027-07-21).
- Marcus Lin (Infra Security): we need you to pull the mirrored copies into our S3 evidence bucket and add these filenames to the matrix.
- Laura Bennett (Legal Ops): will confirm that any redaction/PI masking is acceptable for our compliance review.

Marcus — can you confirm you have capacity to handle the mirror + filename mapping? If yes, I will assign the corresponding Jira ticket and we'll attach the profile ID.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Vendor Onboarding Manager
Redwood Inference
